analysis:
All three changed files are documentation only; no code or control changes are visible in this batch.

- docs/architecture/prefix-cache.md (hunk @@ -126, new lines ~129-152) adds a GLM-5.3 section. It describes GLM5NextPagedSparseState and PagedImmutableSnapshot, and a new layout, native-paged-glm5next-full-state-v1, that persists convolution/recurrence and sparse-page state. SSD prefix cache is said to default on for EigenLabs/GLM-5.3-Flash-MLX-NVFP4-mtp via PrefixCachePolicy.isGLM5NextDefaultModel, with DARKBLOOM_PREFIX_CACHE=0 as the opt-out. This touches T-041 (at-rest cache, SEC-035 accepted risk), A-001 and TB-007. The T-041 detection_hint requires review of changes to the production gate, but the threat model does not list the GLM codec or the new default-on model. I raised one low finding for that gap.
- The same section states GLM stays outside the registered coordinator serving models, and that the codec alone adds no qualified capability. That is consistent with existing scope, but it conflicts mildly with the default-on claim.
- docs/architecture/model-registry.md adds a paragraph on raw GLM discovery quotation: bounded headers and non-weight file sizes, a malformed GLM inventory has no loadable fallback, and only the snapshot tokenizer is supported. It states these checks do not replace catalog/source identity, which is consistent with the existing weight-integrity model (A-004, T-012, T-027).
- docs/architecture/inference.md is a head-only excerpt (lines 1214-1409) with no visible diff and no new security claims. It covers MiMo/Qwen4 ownership, the coordinator channel and the Bonsai revision pins.

The actual code (PrefixCachePolicy, GLM codec, store binding) is not in this batch. The next pass should confirm that the real implementation matches these doc claims: HMAC-only names, no prompt-derived plaintext metadata, a TTL of at most 30 minutes, and the cacheSalt scope.

findings.detail: The new prefix-cache.md text says SSD eligibility now defaults on for the locally selected EigenLabs/GLM-5.3-Flash-MLX-NVFP4-mtp (PrefixCachePolicy.isGLM5NextDefaultModel). It also adds a new layout, native-paged-glm5next-full-state-v1, that persists sparse-page, convolution and recurrence state. T-041's detection_hint treats any loosening of the PrefixCachePolicy production gate as widening the at-rest surface and requires review. T-041's affected_files and sign-off history do not mention the GLM codec or this default-on decision. The same-account TTFT oracle across the 30-minute TTL, the HMAC-named files and the KEK-wipe purge are presumably unchanged. The new state types carry prompt-derived data that is not explicitly covered, and the GLM store binding is not attested in the threat model. Trigger: a GLM-selecting provider writes encrypted checkpoints by default, and an operator or reviewer relies on a threat model that never assessed this model or codec. Fix: add the GLM5Next full-state codec, store files and policy to T-041's affected_files and detection_hint. Record an explicit SEC-035 and per-donation-gate decision for the new default-on model. Confirm that the lookup tags and AAD carry no prompt-derived metadata beyond the keyed tag.
findings.title: Threat model does not cover the new default-on GLM-5.3 encrypted SSD prefix-cache path
